statement.text:
Let X be a class of finite groups that is closed with respect to taking sub-
groups, homomorphic images, and extensions. A subgroup H of a finite group G is
said to be X-submaximal if there exists an embedding of G into a group G∗ such that
G is subnormal in G∗ and H coincides with the intersection of G and an X-maximal
subgroup of G∗ . Suppose that all X-submaximal subgroups of a characteristic sub-
group N of a finite group G are conjugate in N . Does it follow that HN/N is an
X-submaximal subgroup of G/N for every X-submaximal subgroup H of G?
    For normal subgroups N , this is not true even if N is an X-group or if N does
not contain nontrivial X-subgroups. A positive answer is known in the case where N
coincides with the F-radical of G for a Fitting class F.
                                                               D. O. Revin, A. V. Zavarnitsine
